newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares close 2.81 pct higher after U.S. CPI.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares close 2.81 pct higher after U.S. CPI.

text.p: Dutch shares closed sharply higher on Tuesday, rising 2.81 percent after a lower than expected 0.1 percent rise in March U.S. Consumer Price Index data (CPI) soothed worries about a rise in U.S. interest rates.

Dealers said the surge on Wall Street, up 86 points by the time the Amsterdam market closed, had settled nervousness awakened after the U.S. market's steep falls following last Friday's core March U.S. producer prices rise.
The AEX share index, trading seven points higher at around 723.50 before the 1230 GMT CPI release, surged on the data, closing 20.16 points higher at 736.37.
Dealers said trading volumes had been disappointingly small for such a large index move, with big institutional investors still apparently holding back from the market.
"What we've seen today is not institutional investors buying like crazy, I think we've seen some traders caught short and having to cover themselves," said one dealer.

Another said Friday's upcoming options expirations were also making for volatile trading conditions. "There's a lot of professional business coming out of the options exchange -- it's not investors buying," he said. "A gain of nearly three percent isn't normal -- we're out of line with other markets," he added.

Dealers said the market was becoming increasingly speculative and prone to mood swings on interest rate scares. "It's only two trading sessions since the PPI figures, when we all thought rates would go up and now, after the CPI data, there are no inflation worries?" said the dealer.
"Tomorrow we could have a figure and we'll be back looking for another rate hike," said another dealer. "What you want in this market is a crystal ball not a research department.
He added the market needed to consolidate back towards the 700 level, although he acknowledged that if Wall Street held its gain to the close, the AEX would rise again early on Wednesday.
